_comment: Tier-2 for skfem time_dependent#3, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: for time-varying non-homogeneous BCs, update the rhs and re-condense each step; condensing once and reusing leaves the boundary DOFs at their initial values. Ran: heat equation on a 16x16 MeshTri.init_tensor with ElementTriP1 (289 DOFs, 64 boundary DOFs), backward Euler, dt=2e-3, 20 steps, with the wall temperature ramped from 0 to 1, once re-condensing every step and once freezing the condensation from step 0. Printed: the re-condensed run lands its boundary DOFs exactly on the prescribed final value 1.0 (error 0.000e+00) while the frozen run holds every boundary DOF at 0.000000 for the whole run (error 1.000e+00), i.e. stuck at the initial value exactly as claimed. The failure is COMPLETELY SILENT -- empty warning list, finite everywhere, a smooth field -- and it is not confined to the boundary: the interior differs by 100% relative, because the frozen lifting feeds wrong data into the interior equations at every step. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 calls integrate(refresh_bc=True) for the second, pathological run, so it re-condenses with the current wall value every step instead of freezing the condensation from step 0. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 8 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'frozen_boundary_tracks_bc=False', 'frozen_boundary_stuck_at_initial_value=True' and 'interior_is_wrong_too=True' (and emits 'FAIL:'), so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
